text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.76% today, capping a brutal two-week decline of nearly 10%. The drop reflects a broader unwinding of the refinery boom that had driven these stocks higher—a trade that analysts say is now "over." Refineries are running at 95.7% capacity with ample fuel inventories (gasoline and diesel storage both well-stocked), which limits pricing power, while crude oil has pulled back to $89.53 per barrel, eroding margins that refiners need to stay highly profitable.

The geopolitical chaos in the Middle East—tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi strikes on Saudi facilities, and escalating U.S. sanctions on Iran—would normally support oil prices and help refiners. Instead, the market is pricing in a shift: the structural advantage refiners enjoyed during the energy supply crunch appears to have faded, and investors are rotating out of the sector regardless of near-term supply risks.
